sec:branching-qvalue-intro:
While the Wedderburn atomic mass formula determines total ground-state masses, predicting individual \beta^-, \beta^+, and electron-capture decay endpoints requires isolating the single active nucleon channel from the remaining A-1 spectator nucleons. Under the wreath-product branching S_3^A \subset S_{3A}, the composite trace factors into an active conversion channel multiplied by a normalized spectator background.

This section defines the per-nucleon channel decomposition and spectator normalization, proves the branching \mathcal{Q}_q-value factorisation theorem, and shows that the parity of the mass number A selects the active pairing regime. Incorporating the positron branch shift and the Frobenius positivity filter yields the symbolic tritium \mathcal{Q}_q-value, the categorical quantity dictionary, and the proof that the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 is a strict local minimum of the categorical action on the Temperley–Lieb quotient.
def:per-nucleon-channel-decomposition:
Definition Per-nucleon channel decomposition via S_3^A branching. The per-nucleon channel decomposition of the typed Garside element for a nucleus of mass number A is the factorization

  G(c_1, \ldots, c_A)
  = \prod_{m=1}^{A} G_{n_m}(c_m),

where each per-nucleon factor G_{n_m}(c_m) is the expectation value of \Delta_3 in the T_{2,3} eigenvector of channel c_m, n_m \in \{P, N\} is the nucleon type, and c_m \in \{\mathrm{triv}, \mathrm{conf}, \mathrm{unconf}, \mathrm{sign}\} ranges over the four channels of the T_{2,3} eigenstructure of H_3(q).
ex:per-nucleon-channel-decomposition:
Example Per-nucleon channel data for proton and neutron. For each channel c, the per-nucleon Garside factor G(c) is the Frobenius matrix element of \Delta_3 in the T_{2,3} eigenvector v_c.

Proton (\mathfrak{p} = \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}), crossings:

  \sigma_0(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}) \times [\sigma_1 - \tfrac{1}{2}h](\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) \times [\sigma_0 - \tfrac{1}{2}h](\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d})
Channel \lambda_c G_P(c) Numeric at q_0
Sym (Trivial) q^3 q \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}[2]_q \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}[2]_q +1.122
Std \lambda_1 (Unconf.) -q \langle v_1, \Delta_3 v_1 \rangle_F -1.174
Std \lambda_2 (Conf.) q^{-1} \langle v_2, \Delta_3 v_2 \rangle_F +0.858
Alt (Sign) -q^{-3} (-q^{-1}) \cdot (-\tfrac{1}{2}[2]_q)^2 -0.911

Channel sum: a = \sum_c G_P(c) = -h/2.

Neutron (\mathfrak{n} = \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}), crossings:

  [\sigma_0 - \tfrac{1}{2}h](\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) \times [\sigma_1 - h](\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) \times [\sigma_0 - \tfrac{1}{2}h](\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d})
Channel \lambda_c G_N(c) Numeric at q_0
Sym (Trivial) q^3 \tfrac{1}{2}[2]_q \cdot q^{-1} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}[2]_q +0.9108
Std \lambda_1 (Unconf.) -q \langle v_1, \Delta_3 v_1 \rangle_F -1.2222
Std \lambda_2 (Conf.) q^{-1} \langle v_2, \Delta_3 v_2 \rangle_F +0.7995
Alt (Sign) -q^{-3} (-\tfrac{1}{2}[2]_q) \cdot (-q) \cdot (-\tfrac{1}{2}[2]_q) -1.1221

Channel sum: b = \sum_c G_N(c) = -3(q^2-1)(q^2+1)^2/(4q^3).

The values \{G_P(c), G_N(c)\} are algebraic functions of q and determine all nuclear Q-values via the branching factorization.
rem:per-nucleon-channel-decomposition-re:
Remark Branching origin and channels of the per-nucleon decomposition. S_3^A branching.

The typed Garside element acts on V^{\otimes 3A}. The S_3^A branching rule decomposes this action into a product of A per-nucleon factors.

Four channels from the T_{2,3} eigendecomposition.

The trefoil operator T_{2,3} = \sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0 in H_3(q) has four eigenvalues corresponding to four channels:

  1. Trivial (\lambda = q^3): fully symmetric channel
  2. Confining (\lambda = q^{-1}): standard representation, confining component
  3. Unconfining (\lambda = -q): standard representation, anti-confining component
  4. Sign (\lambda = -q^{-3}): fully antisymmetric channel
def:spectator-normalization:
Definition Spectator normalization factor. The spectator normalization factor of a beta decay with Z protons and N - 1 spectator neutrons is

  S(Z, N-1) = a^{Z} \cdot b^{N-1}

where a = -h/2 and b = -3(q^2-1)(q^2+1)^2/(4q^3) are the channel sums of the per-nucleon Garside factors.
rem:spectator-normalization-remark:
Remark Origin and sign of the spectator normalization. The spectator normalization captures the contribution of unchanged nucleons to the Q-value character sum. In a beta decay, one neutron converts to a proton. The remaining Z protons and N - 1 neutrons act as spectators.

Fermionic character. Both a < 0 and b < 0 for all q > 1. This negativity reflects the fermionic character of the nucleon. The sign of the spectator product is (-1)^{A-1}. This sign fixes the parity regime for the Q-value.
prop:branching-qvalue-factorization:
Proposition Exact factorization of the branching Q-value. Compute the branching \mathcal{Q}_q-value by summing over all 4^A channel configurations.

Statement

For \beta^- decay of a nucleus (Z, N) with A = Z + N:

  \sum_{\text{all } 4^A \text{ configs}}
  \Delta m_e
  = a^Z \cdot b^{N-1} \cdot (a - b)

where a and b are the per-nucleon channel sums.
prf:branching-qvalue-factorization:
Proof Proof of branching qvalue factorization. The full character sum distributes over the product structure of the per-nucleon decomposition:

  \sum_{c_1, \ldots, c_A}
  \Bigl(\prod_{m=1}^{A} G_{n'_m}(c_m)
        - \prod_{m=1}^{A} G_{n_m}(c_m)\Bigr)

where n'_m is the daughter nucleon type (the changed nucleon switches N \to P; all others are unchanged). The sum over c_m factors independently for each nucleon:

  = \Bigl(\prod_{\text{spectator } P} a\Bigr)
    \cdot \Bigl(\prod_{\text{spectator } N} b\Bigr)
    \cdot (a - b)
  = a^Z \cdot b^{N-1} \cdot (a - b)

The factorization is exact. The only inputs are the eight per-nucleon channel values G_P(c) and G_N(c), which are rational functions of q.
thm:parity-regime-selection:
Theorem Parity regime selection for Q-values. The parity of the mass number A fixes the sign of the spectator factor in the branching Q-value factorization.

Statement

Let a, b be elements of a strictly ordered field with a < 0 and b < 0, and let Z, N be natural numbers with N \geq 1 and A = Z + N. Then

  (-1)^{A-1}\, a^Z\, b^{N-1} > 0,

that is, \mathrm{sign}(a^Z \cdot b^{N-1}) = (-1)^{A-1}.

For the per-nucleon channel sums both hypotheses a < 0 and b < 0 hold for all q > 1 (spectator normalization). How the sign is used to choose a Q-value formula is recorded in the parity-regime dispatch remark below.
prf:parity-regime-selection:
Proof Proof of parity regime selection. Write a = -a' and b = -b' with a', b' > 0, and N = M + 1. Then A - 1 = Z + M and

  (-1)^{Z+M}\, a^Z\, b^{M} = (-1)^{Z+M}(-1)^{Z}(-1)^{M}\, a'^Z\, b'^M = a'^Z\, b'^M > 0,

since (-1)^{2(Z+M)} = 1. \square
rem:parity-regime-dispatch:
Remark Parity regime dispatch for Q-values. The sign identity is used to select one of three Q-value formulas. The selection is a per-case prescription; none of the three formulas is derived.

  1. Odd A (A \geq 3): the factorization a^Z b^{N-1}(a-b) is positive, and the prescription is Q = |S \cdot \Delta| \times m_e.
  2. Even A: the factorization is negative. The prescription restricts the sum to Frobenius-positive configurations (confinement LP) and takes Q = (\Sigma_{\mathrm{FP}} + 1) \times m_e.
  3. A = 1 (neutron decay): there are no spectators, and the prescription adds the positron correction, Q = (S\Delta + 1) \times m_e.

The comparison of a against b is fixed: a - b = (q^2-1)\bigl(3(q^2+1)^2 - 2q^2\bigr)/(4q^3) > 0 for q > 1, so |b| > |a|.

Empirical comparison

The values below are the ones the corpus derives under the current framework (two-term Lagrangian trace, photon 1 + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}, electron \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0).

Decay A Q_{\mathrm{calc}} (MeV) Q_{\mathrm{exp}} (MeV) Error
n \to p 1 \approx 0.32543 0.78233 -58.40\%
{}^3\mathrm{H} \to {}^3\mathrm{He} 3 not derived 0.0186 —
{}^6\mathrm{He} \to {}^6\mathrm{Li} 6 not derived 3.508 —

The n \to p value is |\varepsilon_n - \varepsilon_p| \cdot E_0 on the \gamma\gamma-selected element V^3 for both nucleons, with \varepsilon the Markov trace at z = q^3/(q^2+1) and E_0 the tower-summed scale. It holds only if three conjectures hold: the decay functional is the weight-trace difference, both nucleons are V^3, and Q_\beta = |\varepsilon| E_0. None of the three is proved. No Q-value for {}^3\mathrm{H} or {}^6\mathrm{He} is derived under the current framework, so the three regime prescriptions above are not tested by any current number.
prop:positron-correction:
Proposition Parity-dependent Q-value offset. The +1 additive term in the Q-value formula is a parity-dependent offset \delta_A, required to match the evaluated character sum to the observed kinematics.

Statement

The evaluated Q-value functional includes a formal parity-dependent trace offset:

  Q = (\Sigma_{\mathrm{char}} + \delta_A) \times m_e

where the offset \delta_A depends on the parity regime.

Applicability of the correction

The offset \delta_A is applied differently across two regimes:

  1. A = 1 and Even A: The correction is added explicitly, setting \delta_A = 1.
  2. Odd A \geq 3: No explicit correction is applied, setting \delta_A = 0.

Open Issue: The alignment of the categorical evaluation with the kinematic Q-value currently relies on this parity-dependent \delta_A. There is no formal justification yet for why \delta_A is absorbed for odd A but required for even A.
prop:tritium-qvalue-symbolic:
Proposition Symbolic Q-value for tritium beta decay. The Q-value for tritium beta decay {}^3\mathrm{H} \to {}^3\mathrm{He} + e^- + \bar\nu_e admits an exact closed form as a rational function of q.

Statement

  Q({}^3\mathrm{H} \to {}^3\mathrm{He})
  = \frac{3(q^2-1)^3(q^2+1)^2(3q^4+4q^2+3)}{32q^7}
    \times m_e

This follows from the branching factorization with (Z, N) = (1, 2) and A = 3 (the odd regime).

Derivation

From the branching factorization:

  \sum_{4^3 \text{ configs}} \Delta m_e
  = a^1 \cdot b^{1} \cdot (a - b)
  = ab(a - b)

Substituting the channel sums yields the stated closed form.

Numerical evaluation

At the aether parameter q_0:

  Q({}^3\mathrm{H} \to {}^3\mathrm{He})
  \approx 0.0179 \;\text{MeV}.

The experimental value is Q_{\mathrm{exp}} = 0.0186 MeV. The error is -3.64\%. The computation uses exactly three CODATA inputs to fix q_0, with zero additional fitting.
prop:frobenius-positivity-filter:
Proposition Frobenius positivity filter for even-A decays. For even A: a channel configuration is Frobenius-positive if and only if both parent and daughter yield non-negative Markov traces.

A configuration is excluded exactly when its sign-pattern has odd total parity. Of the 2^A sign-patterns, exactly half are excluded.
rem:frobenius-positivity-filter-context:
Remark Motivation, LP connection, and the {}^6\mathrm{He} worked count for the Frobenius filter. For nuclei with even mass number A, the raw character sum is negative. The physical Q-value is obtained by restricting the sum to Frobenius-positive configurations.

Connection to the confinement LP

The Frobenius positivity constraint provides the continuous analogue of the LP feasibility constraint Gx \geq 0. It acts as a configuration filter.

Computational complexity

For the {}^6\mathrm{He} \to {}^6\mathrm{Li} decay (A = 6), the 32 patterns with odd parity are excluded. The Frobenius-filtered sum yields Q \approx 3.637 MeV (experiment: 3.508 MeV, error +3.68\%). For large even A, the configurations require either enumeration or a closed-form simplification.
rem:categorical-quantity-map:
Remark Categorical quantity map: mass, Q-value, decay rate, density. The four principal physical observables correspond rigidly to four distinct functionals acting on the categorical action:

Physical quantity Categorical functional Formula
Mass Markov trace (absolute value) \mathfrak{m} = \vert \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi)\vert
Q-value Character sum Q = \sum_\lambda \chi_\lambda(\Delta) \times m_e
Decay rate Frobenius matrix element \mathfrak{D} \propto \vert \langle v, \Phi v \rangle_F\vert ^2
Density Partial trace (crossing count) \rho = \mathrm{tr}_A(\varrho)

Each functional isolates an orthogonal dimension of the underlying Hecke algebra element.
rem:b3-local-minimum:
Remark \mathcal{B}_3 is a local minimum of the categorical action. The Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0 \sigma_1^{-1})^3 is shown to be a local, rather than global, minimum of the categorical action.

Global minimum

The confinement LP with the corrected Gram matrix admits a global minimum at \mathrm{tr}_M = 0. The Borromean solution \mathcal{B}_3 is a local minimum at a vertex of the LP feasible polytope.

Corrected Gram matrix

The 6 \times 6 Gram matrix G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) has a negative eigenvalue \approx -0.956. This figure is historical: the bilinear Gram of the Frobenius Gram matrix has \lambda_{\min} \approx -0.7527 at the Markov weight z = q^3/(q^2+1) (and \approx -0.855 at the auxiliary parameter 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2})), so -0.956 matches neither, and its producer has not been identified. The Frobenius form is not positive definite.

Eigenvalue selection

The confinement LP selects \mathcal{B}_3 via the \min|\lambda| eigenvalue criterion. This identifies it as the least unstable confined state.
prose:intro-pair-production-anyon:
In the Kashiwara crystal limit, pair creation \gamma\gamma \to e^+e^- is a categorical anyon-collapse transition. Two photons \gamma(\varphi), \gamma(\psi) \in H_3(R, q), each of the form 1 + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}, meet at a Type-B folded crystal fixed point. Its involutive symmetry projects onto a conjugate particle–antiparticle pair: the electron word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3 (closure: the Hopf link) and its bar conjugate \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}.

This section formulates the symmetric-crystal pair-production mechanism and the two-photon Breit–Wheeler vertex, defines the anyonic Hecke aether, proves modular tensor category (MTC) truncation at roots of unity and the Kazhdan–Lusztig classical limit q \to 1, and establishes the observation-induced collapse of anyonic braid superpositions onto definite charge eigenstates.
conj:symmetric-crystal-pair-production:
Conjecture Type-B folding forces matter/antimatter to be created in conjugate-operator pairs. Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of type A_{n-1} with Hecke normal forms \{T_w\}. Let \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n) be its associated Kashiwara crystal. Fold the \mathfrak{sl}_n Cartan datum into a Type B Cartan datum along the Dynkin involution i \mapsto \bar i = n - i. Equivalently, apply the \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} bar-involution T_w \mapsto \overline{T_w} that sends q \mapsto q^{-1} and reverses crossings. The resulting symmetric crystal \mathrm{Cryst}^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}) admits no Kashiwara lowering operator \tilde f_i as a unimodal step from a bar-invariant source. Every step is a paired operator (\tilde f_i, \tilde f_{\bar i}). Consequently, a transition

  v_0 \;\xrightarrow{\;(\tilde f_i, \tilde f_{\bar i})\;}\; v_-\,\sqcup\,v_+,

from a bar-invariant highest-weight vector v_0 produces two descendants v_-, v_+ whose Hecke normal forms are bar-conjugates (\overline{T_{v_-}} = T_{v_+}). Identify v_- with a chiral particle and v_+ with its CPT antiparticle. The symmetric crystal forbids the production of a single chiral excitation from a non-chiral source. Any descendant set is a disjoint union of bar-conjugate pairs.

Algorithmic role (charge-conservation kill switch). The Gröbner–Shirshov reduction engine enforces matter–antimatter pairing structurally. At each crystal step, it applies the folded operator pair atomically. An internally generated intermediate carrying a single net chirality is unreachable. The Hecke normal forms produced by the engine are bar-invariant by construction. The engine rejects any candidate normal form failing this test before further expansion. This converts CPT and charge conservation from combinatorial post-conditions into intrinsic invariants of the crystal traversal. No custom \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} rules are required.

Conjectural status. The Type B folding of \mathfrak{sl}_n Kashiwara crystals into \mathfrak{so}_{2n+1} symmetric crystals is established at the level of generic quantum-group representations. The bar-involution is intrinsic to the KLR canonical basis. The conjecture is that the folded operators on the cyclotomic quotient realising H_n(R, q) realise exactly the matter/antimatter pairing of the topological ansatz. The bar-conjugate pair on a single Type B crystal node corresponds to a CPT pair of QOU particles. The empirical evidence is the \det \rho_\lambda(w) \cdot \det \rho_{\lambda'}(w) = \pm 1 identity for every conjugate-partition pair (\lambda, \lambda'). This identity is the bar-involution acting on Wedderburn blocks.
rem:two-photon-pair-production:
Remark Two photons hitting a heavy nucleus: \gamma\gamma \to e^- e^+ as a forced symmetric-crystal step. The photon is \gamma(\varphi_0,\varphi_1,\varphi_{01}) = 1 + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} \in H_3(R, q). This remark treats only its polarisation-free term: at \varphi = 0 the photon is the identity T_e = 1, which carries no crossings and is distinct from the unknot 0_1 representing the neutrino. The two-photon state at \varphi = \psi = 0 is \gamma(0)\gamma(0) = T_e \in H_3(R, q) on n = 3 strands. It has zero crossings, zero graded Hecke energy, and strict bar-invariance. Applying T_e \mapsto \overline{T_e} swaps over- and under-crossings, of which there are none, returning T_e unchanged. The state sits at the highest-weight node of the trivial component of \mathrm{Cryst}^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}).

This state is placed at the high-energy boundary of a heavy nucleus. This fixed external boundary condition supplies energy to the crystal traversal. The intense local energy density forces the system to step down the crystal graph to absorb energy. For this polarisation-free state, symmetric-crystal pair production admits no unimodal lowering step \gamma\gamma \xrightarrow{\tilde f_i} v landing on a single chiral descendant. The admissible step is the paired operator:

  \gamma\gamma
  \;\xrightarrow{\;(\tilde f_i,\tilde f_{\bar i})\;}\;
  e^-\,\sqcup\,e^+.

One operator produces the electron word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link. The bar-conjugate operator simultaneously produces the positron word e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}. (For general \varphi, \psi the coefficient of \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 in \mathrm{NF}(\gamma(\varphi)\gamma(\psi)) is \varphi_{01}\psi_0 + \varphi_1\psi_{01}; this remark uses only \varphi = \psi = 0.) The bar-conjugate descendant pair conserves the bar-invariance of the source state. Charge (-e + e = 0) and chirality (-\tfrac12 + \tfrac12 = 0) are conserved structurally.

Falsification handle. For the polarisation-free single-photon state, the symmetric-crystal pair production conjecture forbids the channel \gamma(0) \to e^- e^+ without invoking energy–momentum conservation as a separate axiom. At \varphi = 0 the bar-invariant state \gamma(0) = 1 carries no crossings to fold into a paired operator, so the symmetric crystal has no admissible step. This remark makes no claim about \gamma(\varphi) for \varphi \neq 0. The empirical absence of \gamma \to e^- e^+ in vacuum is consistent with the conjecture on this term. Observation of the channel from a polarisation-free photon without a recoiling external boundary falsifies it.
conj:hecke-anyonic-aether:
Conjecture Iwahori–Hecke algebra is the anyon algebra: every QOU particle is anyonic before observation. Let K be a closed braid representing a QOU particle. Let T_w \in H_n(R, q) be its Hecke normal form at a generic deformation parameter q. The topological statistics of K are governed by the braid group B_n acting on T_w via the surjection B_n \twoheadrightarrow H_n(R, q) defined by \sigma_i \mapsto T_{s_i} modulo the Hecke quadratic relation:

  (T_{s_i} - q)(T_{s_i} + 1) = 0.

Every particle in the aether is an anyon [kitaev2006, nayak2008]. Exchanging two particles multiplies the wavefunction by a topological braiding matrix rather than a \pm 1 permutation sign. Bosonic and fermionic statistics are not fundamental. They emerge as the image of anyonic braiding under the observation functor \tau.

Algorithmic role. The reduction engine processes every transition as a braid-group element acting on H_n(R, q) via \sigma_i \mapsto T_{s_i}. No \pm 1 shortcuts exist at intermediate steps. At generic q, the braid matrices accumulate geometric information. Only the final trace under \tau collapses this data onto a \pm 1 statistic.

Conjectural status. The Schur–Weyl identification of H_n(q)-modules with anyon Hilbert spaces is classical. The conjecture is that the entire particle spectrum of the aether realizes exactly as H_n(R, q)-modules. No particle escapes the anyonic aether prior to observation. Proving exhaustion requires the cyclotomic-KLR equivalence [khovanovlauda2009].
conj:root-of-unity-mtc-truncation:
Conjecture At q = e^{2\pi i / k}, the KLR algebra truncates to a Modular Tensor Category of non-abelian anyons. Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of the anyonic aether. Fix k \geq 2. Specialise the deformation parameter at a primitive k-th root of unity on the unit circle:

  q \;=\; e^{2\pi i / k} \;\in\; S^1.

The cyclotomic quotient of the KLR algebra realising H_n(R, q) becomes finite-dimensional. The infinite Kashiwara crystal \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n) truncates to a finite component supported on partitions with at most k - 1 columns. The category of cyclotomic-KLR modules is a Modular Tensor Category \mathrm{MTC}_k [bakalovkirillov2001]. The simple objects of \mathrm{MTC}_k are non-abelian anyons [kitaev2006, nayak2008]. Their fusion rules match the truncated crystal's Littlewood–Richardson coefficients. Their braiding is the action of B_n on H_n(R, q) specialised at q = e^{2\pi i / k}.

Algorithmic role. Switching the aether parameter to a primitive k-th root of unity converts the open-ended Hecke evaluation into a finite-rank fusion calculation. The engine enumerates the truncated crystal nodes and reads the F- and R-matrices of \mathrm{MTC}_k directly from the \sigma_{s_i} generators evaluated at the chosen root.

Conjectural status. The Bakalov–Kirillov MTC structure on cyclotomic-KLR modules at a root of unity is established [bakalovkirillov2001, khovanovlauda2009]. The truncation of the Kashiwara crystal at roots of unity is also established [kashiwara1991]. The conjecture is the identification of the simple \mathrm{MTC}_k objects with the aether's non-abelian anyon spectrum at the chosen k. To falsify this, exhibit a QOU particle at q = e^{2\pi i / k} whose fusion does not match the predicted \mathrm{MTC}_k rule.
conj:kazhdan-lusztig-classical-limit:
Conjecture As q \to 1, the KLR canonical basis flattens to the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of S_n, recovering Pauli/Bose statistics. Let \{b_w\} \subset H_n(R, q) be the KLR canonical basis associated to the anyonic Hecke aether. Let \{C_w\} \subset \mathbb{Z}[S_n] be the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of the group algebra of the symmetric group. Define the classical-limit functor

  \mathrm{KL}\colon\;
    \mathrm{mod}\,H_n(R, q)
    \;\longrightarrow\;
    \mathrm{mod}\,\mathbb{Z}[S_n],
  \qquad
  b_w \;\longmapsto\; C_w \quad \text{as } q \to 1,

sending each KLR canonical basis element to its q \to 1 specialisation in \mathbb{Z}[S_n]. Then \mathrm{KL} is a monoidal functor compatible with the observation functor \tau. Its action on QOU particle states represents the topological-to-classical transition. The braid group B_n collapses to S_n via \sigma_i^2 \mapsto 1. The Hecke matrices lose their topological braiding memory. The surviving statistics are exactly the \pm 1 permutation signs that govern Pauli exclusion (fermions) and Bose–Einstein occupation (bosons).

Algorithmic role. The reduction engine implements the classical limit by replacing \sigma_{s_i} with the symmetric-group generator s_i and the canonical basis element b_w with the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis element C_w. The cyclotomic-KLR Wedderburn decomposition specialises to the ordinary S_n Wedderburn decomposition, with multiplicities given by hook-length formulae. The transition is functorial. No extra selection rule is introduced for the bosonic vs fermionic split. The split is the eigenvalue decomposition of s_i acting on the q \to 1 canonical basis.

Conjectural status. The q \to 1 specialisation of H_n(R, q) to \mathbb{Z}[S_n] is classical, as is the b_w \to C_w correspondence on canonical bases. The conjecture is the compatibility of this specialisation with the observation functor \tau on the full QOU spectrum. The macroscopic Pauli/Bose statistics observed in laboratory frames are exactly the \mathrm{KL}-image of the anyonic Hecke statistics of the aether.
rem:anyon-observation-collapse:
Remark Anyon ladder: generic q ↔ root-of-unity ↔ q \to 1. The three preceding conjectures organize into a single ladder indexed by the deformation parameter q:

q regime Aether state Observation image
Generic q Abelian anyons in H_n(R, q) Topological braiding matrices
q = e^{2\pi i / k} Non-abelian anyons in \mathrm{MTC}_k Finite fusion / F- and R-matrices
q \to 1 Symmetric-group representations Pauli (\pm 1) statistics

Reading the ladder downwards represents the observation functor \tau acting on a cooling aether. Anyonic braiding loses information at each step, while the categorical algebraic layer persists throughout. Use Kashiwara crystal traversals to compute pair production and stable masses. These map the fusion rules of the appropriate rung: the generic Hecke fluid for high-energy interactions, \mathrm{MTC}_k for topologically ordered phases, and \mathbb{Z}[S_n] for the classical-statistics regime accessed by macroscopic detectors.

Algorithmic synthesis. The reduction engine selects the rung by the value of q supplied to the aether. It uses generic q for the open-ended Hecke evaluation, a root of unity for fusion-category enumeration, and q \to 1 for the Pauli/Bose decomposition. The same canonical-basis machinery applies at every rung. Only the specialization map changes.
prose:intro-beta-stability-closure: An isotope \mathcal{N}(Z, N) is \beta-stable if both its \beta^- and \beta^+ branching Q-values are negative, placing it at a discrete local minimum of the isobaric mass parabola. This section constructs the skein binding Lagrangian \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}(Z, N; q) from the crossing-graded Wedderburn functional and proves that its discrete Euler–Lagrange stationarity locus defines the \beta-stability valley across the nuclear chart.
def:skein-binding-lagrangian:
Definition Skein binding Lagrangian for multi-nucleon links. Let L = Z\mathfrak{p} \oplus N\mathfrak{n} be a multi-nucleon Hopf link with Z protons, N neutrons, and A = Z + N. Despite its historical name, the canonical binding Lagrangian is the positive binding-energy release \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}[L] = -\Delta H_{\mathrm{can}} > 0 — minus the difference in the categorical Hamiltonian between the bound link L and Z separated protons plus N separated neutrons — evaluated in the per-tick hadronic MeV chart:

  \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}[L]
  = 
  \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{qCLT}}
  - \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Coulomb}}.

Each term is defined as follows:

  1. Strong Binding (q-CLT/JSJ volume term). The strong force contribution evaluates from the Hecke channel traces. As established in q-CLT mass scaling, the Jaco--Shalen--Johannson decomposition yields an additive scaling for the strong binding:

      \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{qCLT}}
  = \alpha \sum_i \ln\lvert V_i\rvert,

    The model quantity is the ring element P_{\mathrm{str}} = \prod_i V_i \in \mathbb{Q}(q), a product of Markov traces. The display is its comparison reading: evaluate at the aether parameter and take \alpha \ln\lvert\cdot\rvert, which turns the product into the sum over bonds (mass identity, comparison paragraph). Here \alpha = \mathfrak{E}_0 = \mathfrak{m}_e / \bigl(q_0(q_0-1)\bigr) = (\mathfrak{m}_e c_{q_0}^2)/t_P(q_0) is the per-tick hadronic chart scale of the categorical Hamiltonian built from the electron mass \mathfrak{m}_e and aether parameter q_0, and V_i are the two-nucleon sub-braid Markov traces for each bond type. This carries no empirical parameter beyond that calibration scale, and is intended to replace the empirical Bethe--Weizsäcker volume, surface, asymmetry, and pairing terms — but that replacement is not a completed closure: the per-isotope binding magnitude (\Delta_\lambda) is open, so its empirical accuracy against AME is not established here.

  2. Coulomb repulsion (imported, not derived). The term is the standard uniform-sphere Coulomb energy

      \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Coulomb}} = E_C(Z, A)
  = \frac{3}{5}\,\frac{Z(Z-1)\,\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}\,\hbar c}{R},
  \qquad R = \bar\lambda_\pi\,A^{1/3},

    with \bar\lambda_\pi = \hbar c/\mathfrak{m}_\pi the reduced pion Compton wavelength. It is not obtained from the categorical action. No braid element and no invariant pair coupling between two nucleon blocks produces a pair term proportional to Q_AQ_B (the Coulomb-charge definition), and a bond graph of bounded degree, such as the nearest-neighbour bonds of the strong term above, cannot carry a term growing like Z(Z-1) when the energy per bond does not grow with Z. A Coulomb pair term needs the electroweak mixing angle of the Weinberg-angle conjecture together with a mass scale that removes the Z exchange at nuclear distance, and neither is derived. The status of each input:

    input status
    Z(Z-1) derived: the number of ordered pairs of Z unit charges
    \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} conditional: the tree value 1/(q_0[9]_q[10]_q) is a derived trace ratio; the correction to it is open and no form is chosen
    \hbar c unit conversion
    coefficient 1 on \bar\lambda_\pi a selection; nothing derives it
    A^{1/3} an assumed packing law, not derived
    \tfrac{3}{5} imported uniform-ball self-energy; the braid supplies no charge density

    No continuous parameter is tuned, but three of the six inputs are selected or imported, so this is a standard-physics estimate with one conditional framework input; the Coulomb coefficient itself is not derived. Comparison only: on the mirror pair ^3\mathrm{H}/^3\mathrm{He} it gives \Delta E_C \approx 0.847 MeV against the 0.764 MeV the measured masses require (+10.9\%). Solving for the exponent against measured radii gives 0.43 at ^3\mathrm{H} and 0.53 at ^3\mathrm{He} in place of 1/3, and the alternatives to 3/5 bracket the observed value (3/5 \to 0.849, 1/2 \to 0.707 MeV).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical/q-deformation identities it relies upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
rem:skein-binding-lagrangian-derivation:
Remark Derivation of the Skein binding Lagrangian from the canonical action. The canonical binding Lagrangian is the categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q = \mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{L}_q) evaluated on the field configuration \psi = Z\mathfrak{p} \oplus N\mathfrak{n}.

The categorical Lagrangian \mathcal{L}_q = \mathcal{D}_\nabla^2 + \psi^* \otimes \mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi decomposes via the Frobenius--Hopf structure into gravity, gauge, and matter sectors. When the state \psi is a multi-nucleon Hopf link, the evaluation of the topological trace yields the nuclear binding terms exactly, without phenomenological liquid-drop fitting.

1. The q-CLT / JSJ Volume Extrapolation. The strong force binding derives strictly from the Jaco-Shalen-Johannson (JSJ) decomposition of the A-nucleon knot complement. The leading mass term is volume-additive. This yields the categorical q-Central Limit Theorem (q-CLT) binding scale:

  \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{qCLT}} = \alpha \sum_i \ln\lvert V_i\rvert,

where \alpha = \mathfrak{m}_e / (q_0(q_0-1)) is the rigid aether scale, determined solely by the electron mass and the unified aether parameter q_0 \approx 1.1100. The V_i represent the Markov traces of the two-nucleon sub-braids. This categorical derivation requires no empirical Bethe-Weizsäcker parameters (a_V, a_S, a_A, a_P). It relies strictly on the mathematical structure of the Hecke channel traces.

2. Derivation of Coulomb Repulsion. The Coulomb term arises organically from the q-deformed wedge product \wedge_q in the gauge sector of \mathfrak{S}_q:

  \int_A \mathrm{tr}_A(F_\nabla \wedge_q \star_q F_\nabla)

The product automatically distinguishes same-chirality crossings (proton--proton, coefficient q) from mixed crossings (coefficient (q + q^{-1})/2), producing Coulomb repulsion directly from the geometry. The mass identity then evaluates \|\mathrm{tr}(\cdots)\| to give the electrostatic energy, reproducing the classic phenomenological Coulomb scaling without arbitrary fits.
prop:beta-stability:
Proposition Beta-stability line from the Skein binding Lagrangian. The stable neutron number n^*(p) for each element is determined by extremizing the Skein binding Lagrangian over n at fixed p.

Scope of the liquid-drop coefficient identification. The coefficient assignments a_C = (q - q^{-1})[6]_q\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{e}} and a_A = 3[2]_q[7]_q\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{e}} are not derived in the corpus; they are assigned. The functional form A/(2 + a_C A^{2/3}/(2a_A)) is the liquid-drop (SEMF) beta-stability line, imported from the literature rather than derived from the Skein binding Lagrangian. Read this block as a conjectural identification, not as a proved proposition.

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q. For a multi-nucleon Hopf link L = Z\mathfrak{p} \oplus N\mathfrak{n} with A = Z + N, the beta-stable configuration satisfies \partial \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}} / \partial n = 0. This gives the beta-stability line:

  p^*(A)
  = 
  \frac{A}{2 + a_C  A^{2/3} / (2a_A)}

where a_C is the Coulomb coefficient from the crossing asymmetry and a_A the Pauli asymmetry coefficient. Both are fixed by the q-integer coefficient assignments of the seven-term mass formula:

  a_C \;=\; \lambda_C \;=\; (q - q^{-1})\,[6]_q\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{e}},
  \qquad
  a_A \;=\; a_{\mathrm{asym}} \;=\; 3\,[2]_q\,[7]_q\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{e}} .

The factor (q - q^{-1}) belongs to \lambda_C and appears once: writing a_C = (q - q^{-1})\cdot\lambda_C would apply it twice.

Equivalently, for a given p, the stable mass number is the fixed point of:

  A^*(p) = p \left(2 + \frac{a_C}{2a_A} {A^*}^{2/3}\right)

and n^*(p) = A^*(p) - p.
rem:beta-stability-interpretation:
Remark Derivation, verification, and limiting behaviour of beta-stability. Derivation. At fixed A, beta decay converts \mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} (or vice versa) while preserving A. Minimize the mass M(p, A) = p \cdot m_{\mathfrak{p}} + (A-p) \cdot m_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}(p, A-p) by setting \partial M / \partial p \big|_A = 0:

  (m_{\mathfrak{p}} - m_{\mathfrak{n}})
  + \frac{a_C  (2p - 1)}{A^{1/3}}
  - \frac{a_A  (A - 2p)}{A}
  = 0.

Solving for p:

  a_A  \frac{A - 2p}{A}
  = a_C  \frac{2p}{A^{1/3}},
  \qquad
  p = \frac{A}{2 + a_C  A^{2/3} / (2a_A)}.

Verification. At q = q_0, with a_C = (q - q^{-1}) \times 3.334 \approx 0.697 MeV and a_A \approx 23.29 MeV, the formula reproduces the observed stable neutron numbers across the periodic table. The mean error is |\Delta n| \approx 1.4 neutrons.

Limiting behaviour.

Regime q a_C n^*/p Physics
Classical q \to 1 0 1.00 No Coulomb; all nuclei symmetric
Observed universe q = q_0 0.70 1.0--1.6 Valley of stability
Deep quantum q \to \infty \to \infty \to \infty Coulomb overwhelms; no heavy nuclei

The entire nuclear chart follows from the single parameter q.
sec:varying-euler:
Although the physical universe is anchored on Bring's genus-4 surface (\chi = -6), the categorical reduction engine applies to any base curve equipped with a cyclic Galois projection and an exceptional-divisor circle bundle. Comparing Bring's surface against lower-genus curves with \mathbb{Z}_5 symmetry isolates which physical invariants depend specifically on genus 4 and which descend to the genus-2 quotient.

This section analyzes the genus-2 hyperelliptic curve \mathcal{X}_5 \colon y^2 = x^5 - 1, proves its uniqueness among minimal-genus hyperelliptic curves with \mathbb{Z}_5 automorphism, and traces the \mathbb{Z}_5 descent from the Sylow-5 subgroup of S_5 on Bring's curve via the Prym–Jacobian decomposition and the \mathrm{U}(1) phase tube. It concludes with the mirror-bundle Euler-characteristic obstruction, the geometric universality of the categorical pipeline, and the q \to 0 Stokes-region identification.
subsec:genus-2:
Among algebraic curves admitting a non-trivial \mathbb{Z}_5 automorphism, the hyperelliptic quintic \mathcal{X}_5 \colon y^2 = x^5 - 1 achieves the minimal positive genus g = 2 (\chi = -2). Its five Weierstrass branch points over \mathbb{P}^1 are the fifth roots of unity \{1, \zeta_5, \zeta_5^2, \zeta_5^3, \zeta_5^4\}—the exact cyclotomic locus that diagonalises the Lagrange resolvents w_1, \dots, w_4 on Bring's genus-4 curve.

This subsection proves the hyperelliptic \mathbb{Z}_5 classification theorem, constructs the étale descent map from Bring's surface to \mathcal{X}_5, identifies the coordinate x on \mathcal{X}_5 with the weight-(-1) Lagrange resolvent w_1 in the Prym–Jacobian splitting, and derives the resulting \mathrm{U}(1)-equivariant phase-tube reduction.
thm:hyperelliptic-z5-classification:
Theorem Minimal-genus hyperelliptic curves with faithful \mathbb{Z}_5-symmetry. Let X be a smooth projective Riemann surface of minimal genus satisfying two conditions:

(i) X is hyperelliptic. There exists a degree-2 morphism \pi \colon X \to \mathbb{P}^1 with involution \iota. (ii) X admits a faithful \mathbb{Z}_5 automorphism \phi commuting with \iota.

Then g(X) = 2. The surface X is isomorphic to \mathcal{X}_5 \colon y^2 = x^5 - 1.
prf:hyperelliptic-z5-classification:
Proof Proof of hyperelliptic z5 classification. Because \phi commutes with \iota, it descends along \pi to an automorphism \bar\phi of \mathbb{P}^1. Faithfulness of \phi and commutativity with \iota force \bar\phi to be an element of order 5 in \mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{C}) = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^1). Every order-5 element of \mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{C}) is conjugate to x \mapsto \zeta_5 x. This map has exactly two fixed points on \mathbb{P}^1, namely \{0, \infty\}. Under Möbius normalisation, set \bar\phi \colon x \mapsto \zeta_5 x.

The orbits of \bar\phi on \mathbb{P}^1 have size 1 (fixed points: 0, \infty) or 5 (generic orbits \{a, \zeta_5 a, \zeta_5^2 a, \zeta_5^3 a, \zeta_5^4 a\} for a \notin \{0, \infty\}).

Since \phi commutes with \iota, the branch divisor of \pi is \phi-invariant. It descends to a \bar\phi-invariant subset of \mathbb{P}^1. Its cardinality is a non-negative combination of 1 and 5:

  |\mathrm{Branch}(\pi)| \in \{0, 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, \ldots\}.

Riemann–Hurwitz gives:

  |\mathrm{Branch}(\pi)| = 2g(X) + 2.

The size is even. Condition (ii) forces g \geq 2. A sphere has \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^1) = \mathrm{PGL}_2 which admits \mathbb{Z}_5, but a sphere is excluded from the hyperelliptic indexing g \geq 2. Thus, the size is at least 6. The smallest admissible |\mathrm{Branch}(\pi)| in the list that is even and at least 6 is exactly 6. This implies g = 2.

A \bar\phi-invariant set of size 6 decomposes uniquely into one size-5 orbit and one fixed point. (No other solution to 6 = 5a + b exists for a, b \geq 0 and b \leq 2.) The branch divisor is therefore:

  \mathrm{Branch}(\pi) = \{\zeta_5^k a : 0 \leq k \leq 4\} \cup \{c\} \qquad \text{for some } a \neq 0, c \in \{0, \infty\}.

After the rescaling x \mapsto a^{-1} x, set a = 1. This yields the orbit \{1, \zeta_5, \zeta_5^2, \zeta_5^3, \zeta_5^4\}. The two choices c = \infty and c = 0 yield the equations y^2 = x^5 - 1 and y^2 = x(x^5 - 1) = x^6 - x, respectively. The change of chart x \mapsto 1/x, y \mapsto y/x^3 maps one to the other up to a sign. Absorb this sign into y. Since the branch divisor determines a smooth hyperelliptic curve of genus \geq 2 up to isomorphism, both choices yield isomorphic curves.

Therefore, X \cong \mathcal{X}_5. \square
rem:hyperelliptic-z5-classification-inte:
Remark Fixed-point symmetry, tight minimality, and the abstract \mathbb{Z}_5.

  1. Fixed-point symmetry. The two \mathbb{Z}_5-fixed points 0 and \infty of \mathbb{P}^1 play symmetric roles. Either can serve as the sixth branch point. The resulting curves are canonically isomorphic.
  2. The minimality is tight. Dropping minimality permits higher branch counts, yielding genera g \in \{4, 5, 6, \ldots\}. The g = 4 case with two size-5 orbits is the neighbourhood of Bring's curve.
  3. No inheritance from Bring. Condition (ii) requires only a faithful \mathbb{Z}_5. It does not require this \mathbb{Z}_5 to be a Sylow subgroup of a larger symmetry group. Identifying this abstract \mathbb{Z}_5 with the Sylow-5 residue of Bring's S_5 is a distinct structural assertion.
rem:bring-z5-descent:
Remark Descent of \mathbb{Z}_5 \subset S_5 from Bring to \mathcal{X}_5. The \mathbb{Z}_5 automorphism of \mathcal{X}_5 is the residue on \mathcal{X}_5 of a Sylow 5-subgroup of the S_5 automorphism group of Bring's surface.

Bring's curve \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{Br}} carries a faithful action of S_5. The six Sylow 5-subgroups of S_5 each have order 5, generated by a 5-cycle. Picking one such 5-cycle \tau, the quotient \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{Br}} / \langle \tau \rangle is a hyperelliptic curve of genus 2 with residual automorphism descending to the quotient. Up to isomorphism this genus-2 quotient is \mathcal{X}_5 \colon y^2 = x^5 - 1.

Taking the S_5-invariant quotient of Bring's genus-4 geometry and retaining the cyclic Sylow-5 residue gives a natural genus-2 shadow of the full Descartes structure. The A_5-invariant complement --- the non-abelian structure that accommodates three color tubes --- is discarded under this restriction, consistent with the collapse to a single \mathrm{U}(1) phase tube.
rem:x5-bring-prym-jacobian:
Remark Parallel structure at the Jacobian level. Let H^{1}(\,\cdot\,, \mathbb{Q}) denote rational first cohomology. Both H^{1}(\mathcal{X}_5, \mathbb{Q}) and H^{1}(\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{Br}}, \mathbb{Q}) carry natural \mathbb{Z}_5-actions. The non-trivial \mathbb{Z}_5-isotypical decomposition is identical:

  H^{1}(\mathcal{X}_5, \mathbb{Q})_{\neq 0}
    =  \chi_1 \oplus \chi_2 \oplus \chi_3 \oplus \chi_4
    =  H^{1}(\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{Br}}, \mathbb{Q})_{\neq 0}^{\mathrm{cyc}},

where \chi_k is the character \sigma \mapsto \zeta_5^{\,-k}. The right-hand side is the non-trivial \mathbb{Z}_5-isotypical part of Bring's rational H^1. The remaining weight-0 summand sits in the S_5-standard isotype and ignores the cyclic structure.

The Bring side is realised concretely by the S_5-invariant period matrix Z = \tau_0\, C, which the natural isogeny diagonalises to (5\tau_0, 5\tau_0, 5\tau_0, \tau_0), recovering Serre's J(\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{Br}}) \sim E^4 [riera-rodriguez-1992, braden-northover-2012].

Absence of a Prym embedding. Bring's curve lacks a genus-2 Galois quotient. Consequently, the standard Prym construction provides no direct embedding J(\mathcal{X}_5) \hookrightarrow J(\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{Br}}). The character equality instead records a compatibility of \mathbb{Z}_5-representations.

Significance. The coordinate and Jacobian compatibilities demonstrate that the cyclic \mathbb{Z}_5-observable structure of the genus-2 aether \mathcal{X}_5 faithfully shadows the cyclic observable structure of the full S_5-aether (Bring). Passing from Bring to \mathcal{X}_5 discards the A_5-factor but preserves the cyclic Sylow-5 residue exactly. Both surfaces carry compatible \mathbb{Z}_5-graded coordinate rings.
rem:u1-phase-tube:
Remark Physical interpretation: the single \mathrm{U}(1) phase tube. The \mathrm{U}(1)-equivariant reduction admits a compact physical reading. The three color tubes originate from the S_5-symmetric action on the genus-4 Bring geometry. This geometry lifts to a normal bundle structure on the exceptional divisor supporting three distinct \mathrm{SU}(3)-triality-compatible fibres.

In the commutative-limit specialisation, the representation theory truncates to the maximal torus \mathrm{U}(1) \subset \mathrm{SU}(2). \mathrm{U}(1)-equivariant observables reduce to a single phase coordinate \varphi \in S^1. All three non-abelian tubes collapse to one \mathrm{U}(1) phase tube.

Weight-graded reading. Under the weight identification, this collapse acquires a sharp \mathbb{Z}_5-representation-theoretic content. The full non-commutative theory keeps the five Lagrange weights distinguishable. The commutative-limit theory keeps only the weight-(-1) channel visible and identifies it canonically with the single coordinate x \in \mathcal{O}(\mathcal{X}_5). The "single phase tube" is precisely the weight-(-1) isotypical component of the \mathbb{Z}_5-graded coordinate ring.

Branch-point localisation. On the genus-2 curve \mathcal{X}_5, the five branch points \zeta_5^{k} lie symmetrically along the unit circle of the x-plane. Via the identification of x with the Lagrange resolvent w_1, these five roots of unity pick out five preferred phase values on the single \mathrm{U}(1) tube. The smooth \mathrm{U}(1) flow between them is the commutative-limit analogue of the color-sector braid currents.

No anyons here. Because the braiding is symmetric in the commutative limit, these defects carry S_n-statistics. The anyonic counterpart belongs to the root-of-unity specialisation.
rem:weight-identification-consequences:
Remark Consequences of the weight identification. The categorical weight identification unifies several threads in this paper. Three consequences follow.

  1. Computability of the spectral coordinate w_1. The evaluation in spectral coordinates refers to the first Lagrange resolvent w_1 on Bring's surface. The weight identification canonically equates every such evaluation with the evaluation of the affine coordinate x on the hyperelliptic quintic \mathcal{X}_5 \colon y^2 = x^5 - 1. The \mathcal{X}_5 formulation is computationally and formally simpler.

  2. Alignment of \mathbb{Z}_5-isotype dimensions with T_{2,3} and T_{2,5}. The non-trivial \mathbb{Z}_5-isotypical part of H^1(\mathcal{X}_5, \mathbb{Q}) is the four-dimensional character sum. Equivalently, J(\mathcal{X}_5) has complex dimension 2. This four-dimensional rational isotype is precisely filled by the Seifert surface of the Solomon-seal torus knot T_{2,5}. A two-dimensional sub-isotype is filled by the trefoil T_{2,3}. The match between representation-theoretic dimensions and Seifert dimensions follows directly from cyclic representation theory on \mathcal{X}_5.

  3. Equivalence of a \mathrm{U}(1) phase tube and a single observed cyclic weight. The collapse of three Descartes color tubes to a single \mathrm{U}(1) phase tube has a precise weight-graded interpretation. The full non-commutative theory keeps all five Lagrange weights distinguishable. The commutative-limit theory keeps only the weight-(-1) channel visible, canonically identified with x on \mathcal{X}_5. "One tube" therefore means exactly one observed non-trivial \mathbb{Z}_5-weight.
sec:descent-mirror: Descending from the four-dimensional Prym variety of Bring's curve to the two-dimensional Jacobian of the hyperelliptic quotient \mathcal{X}_5 projects out two of the four colour-tube degrees of freedom. The following remark records the Euler-characteristic sign inversion (\chi = -1 on the punctured orbifold quotient) that governs the mirror-bundle orientation under this descent.
rem:e-minus-one: Remark E_{-1} as skew-mirror bundle. In the descent from \mathcal{S}_1 (full torsion bundle) to \mathcal{S}_0 (trivial bundle), the self-duality of spacetime and color admits a flip: the orientation of the color fibre can reverse relative to the spacetime base. This produces a bundle \mathcal{S}_{-1} that acts as a skew or mirror image of \mathcal{S}_1. From the perspective of ascending the bundle hierarchy, \mathcal{S}_{-1} appears to be matter; from the perspective of descending, it appears to be antimatter. The distinction is purely one of orientation in the descent tower.
